description: Dependency-free synchronous Python Server-Sent Events (SSE) parser for streaming HTTP responses from requests, urllib3, and httpx. Install sseclient-py and import sseclient. Parses byte chunks into events with data, event, id, and retry fields; useful for HTTP event feeds and SSE-framed AI application responses. Requires Python 3.11 or newer.
rules: Install the PyPI package sseclient-py and import sseclient. The separate package named sseclient has a different API.
Pass an existing synchronous iterable of byte chunks to sseclient.SSEClient and iterate client.events(). Do not pass a URL or an async iterator; the parser does not open HTTP connections.
Use requests responses with stream=True, urllib3 response.stream(), or synchronous httpx response.iter_bytes(). Install your chosen HTTP client separately; sseclient-py has no runtime dependencies.

The HTTP client owns authentication, request methods, status checks, timeouts, and cleanup. Use its context manager or cleanup API; SSEClient.close() requires the supplied source to have a close() method.
event.data is text; decode JSON in the application. Named events are exposed as event.event, which defaults to 'message'. event.retry is field text, not an automatically applied delay.

Manage reconnection and backoff in the application. Resume with Last-Event-ID only when the server supports it; ID-only updates are not exposed and duplicate-free delivery is not guaranteed. Replay POST requests only when safe.
This library parses SSE framing; it is not a Model Context Protocol (MCP) SDK and does not implement JSON-RPC or complete MCP HTTP transport behavior.
